newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Proton hints at listing of Lotus.
newsitem.headline: Proton hints at listing of Lotus.

text.p: Malaysian carmaker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton) on Friday hinted that it may seek to list its British subsidiary, Group Lotus Ltd.
"I cannot confirm this as yet, but in the long run why not?" Proton chairman Saleh Sulong said when asked by reporters on speculation that the company may be looking to list Lotus.
He did not give other details at a news conference after the release of Proton's 1996/97 earnings.
Saleh said Lotus was very much involved in the design of a new Proton car model.
Proton and its late key-shareholder, Yahaya Ahmad, bought an 80 percent stake in Lotus for 51 million sterling (then $82.88 million) in October last year.
Proton's chief executive officer Tengku Mahaleel Tengku Ariff said Proton had completed designs for the completely "Malaysian-made" car.
"We have designed our own model. It is going into the final model fix. That has been approved by the board,' he said.
